## Motivation

Each data iteration changes two things at once: the number of occurrence
points, and their geocoding quality. iter0 is public data (noisy),
iter1 adds presences and removes some bad geocodes, and the 2026 field
data adds more vetted presences. A direct comparison of per-iteration
niche estimates confounds *size* with *purity*.

This document estimates the realized niche with one-class SVM
hypervolumes (Blonder's `hypervolume_svm`) and sets up two panels:

- **Panel A** — three as-observed hypervolumes, one per iteration. The
  descriptive, observational story.
- **Panel B** — rarefaction on the clean 2026 universe. Isolates the
  size effect, estimates the asymptotic volume, and reports how much of
  it the current sample captures.

A later Panel C (purity, with-and-without known-bad points at matched
n) reuses the `point_status` bookkeeping created below but is not
executed here.

## Setup

Freeze SVM knobs once; the same `(nu, gamma)` is used for every fit so
nothing downstream depends on a tuning decision.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(hypervolume)
library(terra)

svm_nu    <- 0.05
svm_gamma <- 0.5
```

```{r}
# ---- synthetic test data ---------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS, exclude = "select")

set.seed(42)

env_vars <- paste0("env", 1:4)

# two modes in 4D env space; a mild shared correlation structure
Sigma <- matrix(0.3, 4, 4); diag(Sigma) <- 1
mu_a  <- c(-1.5, -1.5,  0.5,  0.0)
mu_b  <- c( 1.5,  1.5, -0.5,  0.2)

draw_clean <- function(n) {
  k <- rbinom(1, n, 0.5)
  rbind(mvrnorm(k,     mu_a, Sigma),
        mvrnorm(n - k, mu_b, Sigma)) |>
    as_tibble(.name_repair = ~ env_vars)
}

draw_bad <- function(n) {
  # "bad geocodes" land in random env space, uniform over a wide box
  matrix(runif(n * 4, -4, 4), ncol = 4) |>
    as_tibble(.name_repair = ~ env_vars)
}

# clean universe of 2026 points
clean_2026 <- draw_clean(300) |>
  mutate(point_id = paste0("c", row_number()), iter = "iter2026")

# iter1 = subsample of clean 2026 + a few bad points
iter1_clean <- slice_sample(clean_2026, n = 150) |>
  mutate(iter = "iter1")
iter1_bad   <- draw_bad(15) |>
  mutate(point_id = paste0("b1_", row_number()), iter = "iter1")

# iter0 = subsample of iter1_clean + more bad points
iter0_clean <- slice_sample(iter1_clean, n = 80) |>
  mutate(iter = "iter0")
iter0_bad   <- draw_bad(20) |>
  mutate(point_id = paste0("b0_", row_number()), iter = "iter0")

occs_env <- bind_rows(iter0_clean, iter0_bad,
                      iter1_clean, iter1_bad,
                      clean_2026) |>
  select(iter, point_id, all_of(env_vars))
```

## Environmental axes from a seed SDM

Pulling the top four variables from a saved SDM so this document stays
synchronized with the modeling pipeline. When the final cleaned-data
SDM is fit, replace `results/sdm_seed_top.rds` and rerun; nothing else
changes.

```{r env-vars}
seed_model <- read_rds("results/sdm_seed_top.rds")

env_vars <- seed_model |>
  varImp() |>                    # swap for your SDM's accessor
  as_tibble() |>
  slice_max(Importance, n = 4) |>
  pull(Variable)
```

## Occurrences and pooled standardization

One long tibble with an `iter` label. Scaling is done across the pooled
rows so the three iterations live in the same standardized space and
overlaps are meaningful.

```{r occs}
env_stack <- rast("data/env_stack.tif")[[env_vars]]

occs <- bind_rows(
  read_csv("data/occ_iter0.csv")    |> mutate(iter = "iter0"),
  read_csv("data/occ_iter1.csv")    |> mutate(iter = "iter1"),
  read_csv("data/occ_iter2026.csv") |> mutate(iter = "iter2026")
) |>
  select(iter, point_id, lon, lat)

occs_env <- occs |>
  bind_cols(terra::extract(env_stack, as.matrix(occs[, c("lon", "lat")]))) |>
  drop_na(all_of(env_vars)) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(env_vars), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
```

## Point bookkeeping and the clean universe

`point_status` tags each unique `point_id` by its iteration membership
pattern. Points that were present in iter0 but dropped by iter1 are
"removed_iter0_to_iter1"; the same logic defines
"removed_iter1_to_2026". Everything surviving to iter2026 is treated as
the clean universe for Panel B's rarefaction.

```{r bookkeeping}
point_status <- occs_env |>
  group_by(point_id) |>
  summarise(
    in_iter0    = any(iter == "iter0"),
    in_iter1    = any(iter == "iter1"),
    in_iter2026 = any(iter == "iter2026"),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      !in_iter1    &  in_iter0 ~ "removed_iter0_to_iter1",
      !in_iter2026 &  in_iter1 ~ "removed_iter1_to_2026",
      in_iter2026              ~ "kept_clean",
      TRUE                     ~ "other"
    )
  )

clean_pool <- occs_env |>
  filter(iter == "iter2026") |>
  semi_join(filter(point_status, status == "kept_clean"), by = "point_id") |>
  distinct(point_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

## Panel A: three as-observed hypervolumes

```{r panel-a-fits}
hv_fits <- occs_env |>
  select(iter, all_of(env_vars)) |>
  nest(data = all_of(env_vars)) |>
  mutate(
    hv = map2(data, iter, ~ hypervolume_svm(
      as.matrix(.x), name = .y,
      svm.nu = svm_nu, svm.gamma = svm_gamma, verbose = FALSE
    ))
  )

panel_a_volumes <- hv_fits |>
  mutate(volume = map_dbl(hv, get_volume)) |>
  select(iter, volume)
```

### Pairwise overlap

```{r panel-a-overlaps}
panel_a_overlaps <- hv_fits |>
  select(iter, hv) |>
  (\(x) inner_join(x, x, by = character(), suffix = c("_a", "_b")))() |>
  filter(iter_a < iter_b) |>
  mutate(
    stats = map2(hv_a, hv_b, ~ hypervolume_overlap_statistics(
      hypervolume_set(.x, .y, check.memory = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
    ))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    jaccard  = map_dbl(stats, "jaccard"),
    sorensen = map_dbl(stats, "sorensen")
  ) |>
  select(iter_a, iter_b, jaccard, sorensen)
```

## Panel B: rarefaction on the clean universe

### Reference hypervolume

The full-clean-pool fit serves as the comparison "truth" that each
subsampled fit is scored against. Same knobs as Panel A.

```{r reference-hv}
hv_reference <- hypervolume_svm(
  as.matrix(clean_pool[, env_vars]),
  name = "reference_full",
  svm.nu = svm_nu, svm.gamma = svm_gamma, verbose = FALSE
)

n_full <- nrow(clean_pool)
```

### Bootstrap grid

The `n_sample` ladder is a placeholder; replace with the real
`n_iter0`, `n_iter1`, `n_full`, plus a few interpolated anchors. Drop
`replicate` to 25 for a dry run; 100 is where the quantile bands
usually tighten.

```{r bs-grid}
bs_grid <- expand_grid(
  n_sample  = c(20, 40, 80, 160, n_full),
  replicate = 1:100
)
```

### Unified bootstrap worker

One draw per replicate feeds the hypervolume fit, the overlap-with-
reference, and the per-axis 95% range used by the honest-complement
diagnostic. Keeping all three in the same worker guarantees they share
the same subsample.

```{r fit-one}
fit_one <- function(n_sample, replicate) {
  draw <- slice_sample(clean_pool, n = n_sample, replace = FALSE)

  hv <- hypervolume_svm(
    as.matrix(draw[, env_vars]),
    name = paste0("n", n_sample, "_r", replicate),
    svm.nu = svm_nu, svm.gamma = svm_gamma, verbose = FALSE
  )

  ov <- hypervolume_overlap_statistics(
    hypervolume_set(hv, hv_reference, check.memory = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
  )

  axis_ranges <- draw |>
    summarise(across(all_of(env_vars),
                     ~ diff(quantile(.x, c(.025, .975))))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "axis", values_to = "range_q95")

  tibble(
    volume   = get_volume(hv),
    jaccard  = ov["jaccard"],
    sorensen = ov["sorensen"],
    axes     = list(axis_ranges)
  )
}
```

### Run the grid

Cache this chunk so iterating on the asymptote fit and the plots does
not retrigger every SVM fit.

```{r bs-run, cache=TRUE}
bs_results <- bs_grid |>
  mutate(result = map2(n_sample, replicate, fit_one, .progress = TRUE)) |>
  unnest(result)

bs_axes <- bs_results |>
  select(n_sample, replicate, axes) |>
  unnest(axes)
```

## Completeness: asymptote fits on volume vs n

Fit both `SSasymp` (asymptotic regression) and `SSmicmen`
(Michaelis-Menten). MM approaches its asymptote more slowly, so the two
bracket the completeness estimate; report the range.

```{r completeness}
volume_by_n <- bs_results |>
  group_by(n_sample) |>
  summarise(volume = mean(volume), .groups = "drop")

fit_asymp  <- nls(volume ~ SSasymp(n_sample, Asym, R0, lrc), data = volume_by_n)
fit_micmen <- nls(volume ~ SSmicmen(n_sample, Vm, K),        data = volume_by_n)

v_full <- bs_results |> filter(n_sample == n_full) |> pull(volume) |> mean()

completeness <- tibble(
  model        = c("asymp", "micmen"),
  v_inf        = c(coef(fit_asymp)["Asym"], coef(fit_micmen)["Vm"]),
  v_at_n_full  = v_full
) |>
  mutate(completeness = v_at_n_full / v_inf)
```

## Per-axis range curves (honest-complement diagnostic)

Hypervolume plateau can be an SVM-trim artifact: `svm.nu` discards a
fixed fraction of points regardless of n, so the boundary stops
chasing new extremes even if the data keep extending. The per-axis
95%-range at each n is the diagnostic. If the hypervolume curve
flattens while axis ranges keep climbing, the completeness number is
optimistic.

```{r axis-curves}
axis_curves <- bs_axes |>
  group_by(axis, n_sample) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(range_q95),
    lo   = quantile(range_q95, .025),
    hi   = quantile(range_q95, .975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Outputs

- `panel_a_volumes`, `panel_a_overlaps` — observational panel.
- `bs_results` — long table of volume, Jaccard-with-reference,
  Sorensen-with-reference per `(n_sample, replicate)`.
- `completeness` — one row per asymptote model; the pair gives the
  reportable range.
- `axis_curves` — per-env-axis 95%-range at each n for the
  diagnostic plot.

## Known caveats

- **SVM-nu behavior.** Because `svm.nu` trims a fixed fraction of
  points at every n, SVM-based completeness tends to look higher than
  the KDE-based equivalent. Report the estimator explicitly in
  methods.
- **Reference as asymptote.** The reference hypervolume is the full
  clean-pool fit, not a true asymptote. If the volume curve has not
  plateaued at `n_full`, overlap-with-reference is still interpretable
  as "fraction of the current-best estimate recovered," but should
  not be read as "fraction of the true niche."
- **Correlated env axes.** If the seed SDM's top four variables are
  collinear, consider pre-pruning with `caret::findCorrelation` before
  freezing `env_vars`.
